'''Annie Pardo Cemo''' (born 6 June 1940) is a Mexican cell biologist specializing in the study of the [[extracellular matrix]]. She is a member of the [[Sistema Nacional de Investigadores]] and received the [[National Prize for Arts and Sciences (Mexico)|National Prize for Arts and Sciences]] in 2023. She is the mother of Mexican President [[Claudia Sheinbaum|Claudia Sheinbaum Pardo]].

== Early life ==
Annie Pardo Cemo was born in [[Mexico City]] on 6 June 1940.<ref>{{Cite web |date=12 November 2024 |title=Annie Pardo Cemo, la mamá de Claudia Sheinbaum, fue espiada por el Movimiento del 68 |url=https://www.sdpnoticias.com/mexico/quien-es-annie-pardo-cemo-mama-de-claudia-sheinbaum |access-date=12 September 2025 |website=sdpnoticias |language=es}}</ref> Her parents, Mati Magdalena Semo Calev and Jose Pardo Benjaminoff, were [[Sephardic Jews]] from [[Sofia|Sofia, Bulgaria]].<ref>https://forward.com/news/622618/mexico-president-claudia-sheinbaum-jewish-family-holocaust/</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Judío |first=Enlace |date=18 December 2018 |title=Judíos y científicos. La familia de Claudia Sheinbaum |url=https://www.enlacejudio.com/2018/12/17/judios-y-cientificos-la-familia-de-claudia-sheinbaum/ |access-date=12 September 2025 |website=Enlace Judío |language=es}}</ref>  As a result of the [[Bulgaria during World War II#Holocaust|persecution of Jews in Bulgaria]], Pardo's parents emigrated to [[Mandatory Palestine]] and then they arrived in [[Mexico]] shortly before her birth.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Silverstein |first=Andrew |url=https://forward.com/news/622618/mexico-president-claudia-sheinbaum-jewish-family-holocaust|title=Exclusive: Mexico’s new Jewish president has not been telling the truth about her family’s Holocaust story|access-date=20 April 2025|date=14 June 2024|publisher=Forward}}</ref><ref name=":0" />

In 1960, she married chemical engineer [[Carlos Sheinbaum Yoselevitz]], with whom she had three children: Julio, [[Claudia Sheinbaum|Claudia]], and Adriana.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ruidoenlared.com/quien-es/familia-de-claudia-sheinbaum-quienes-son/|title=Familia de Claudia Sheinbaum: ¿quiénes son?|accessdate=7 July 2023|last=Soriano|first=Brenda|date=16 February 2023|website=Ruido en la Red|language=es}}</ref> The couple participated in the [[Mexican Movement of 1968]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://heraldodemexico.com.mx/nacional/2022/6/19/quien-es-carlos-yoselevitz-el-padre-de-claudia-sheinbaum-que-le-inculco-la-pasion-por-el-activismo-414730.html|title=¿Quién es Carlos Yoselevitz?: el padre de Claudia Sheinbaum que le inculcó la pasión por el activismo|accessdate=7 July 2023|date=19 June 2022|website=El Heraldo de México|language=es}}</ref>

== Academic career ==
Annie Pardo studied biology at the [[School of Sciences, UNAM|Faculty of Sciences]] of the [[National Autonomous University of Mexico]]. She also completed her master's and doctoral degrees in [[biochemistry]] at the same university. She conducted research stays at the American universities of  [[Washington University in St. Louis]]; at the [[University of Illinois Chicago]], and at the pathology department of the [[Baylor College of Medicine]] in [[Houston]], [[Texas]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://diariojudio.com/comunidad-judia-mexico/annie-pardo-semo-academica-y-biologa-investigadora-de-la-matriz-extracelular/7339/|title=Annie Pardo Semo, académica y Bióloga Investigadora de la Matriz Extracelular|accessdate=7 July 2023|date=1 October 2013|website=Diario Judío México|language=es}}</ref>

In 1980, she founded the biochemistry research laboratory at the Faculty of Sciences of UNAM. She was a "C-level" professor at the Faculty of Sciences of the [[National Autonomous University of Mexico]] and was named a "level III researcher" of the Sistema Nacional de Investigadores.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://dgapa.unam.mx/index.php/semblanzas-emeritos-anio-perpae-2015/semblanzas-2013-perpae/326-pardo-cemo-annie|title=Pardo Cemo, Annie|accessdate=7 July 2023|website=dgapa.unam.mx}}</ref>

In May 2023, she received the National Prize for Arts and Sciences in the category of physical-mathematical and natural sciences for "her research in biochemistry, lung diseases, and aging studies".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.elfinanciero.com.mx/nacional/2023/05/17/annie-pardo-mama-claudia-sheinbaum-quien-es-y-cual-es-su-trayectoria/|title=PERFIL: Annie Pardo, la mamá de Claudia Sheinbaum ganadora del Premio Nacional de Ciencias|accessdate=7 July 2023|date=17 May 2023|website=El Financiero|language=es}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.jornada.com.mx/notas/2023/05/16/ciencia-y-tecnologia/otorgara-sep-galardones-por-el-premio-nacional-de-ciencias-2022/|title=La Jornada - Otorgará SEP a Annie Pardo el Premio Nacional de Ciencias 2022|accessdate=7 July 2023|website=www.jornada.com.mx}}</ref>

== Controversies ==

=== Panama Papers ===
Annie Pardo Cemo's name appeared in the [[Panama Papers]], a leak of documents related to companies registered in [[Tax haven|tax havens]]. According to the documentation, Pardo Cemo opened multiple bank accounts between March 1990 and November 2009 in various tax havens, and had links to the company JAEM Ltd., a consortium based in the [[British Virgin Islands]] considered "an entity facilitating tax evasion and fortune concealment through tax havens".<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://offshoreleaks.icij.org/nodes/12013630|title=ANNIE PARDO SEMO {{!}} ICIJ Offshore Leaks Database|accessdate=7 July 2023|website=offshoreleaks.icij.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ciudadanosenred.com.mx/politica/annie-pardo-madre-de-claudia-sheinbaum-vinculada-a-panama-papers/|title=Annie Pardo, madre de Claudia Sheinbaum, vinculada a Panama Papers|accessdate=7 July 2023|date=15 June 2021|website=Ciudadanos en Red}}</ref>

=== Actual birthplace controversy and allegation of forged documents ===

According to official Mexican birth registry documents, Annie Pardo Cemo was born in Mexico City on 6 June 1940, but this was a late registration that is dated to have happened on 31 December 1940 (6 months and 3 weeks after her birth), which is the last day of the year and the final entry in the 1940 birth register—a fact that could suggest her entry was improperly included in the 1940 register, given that documentation shows her family did not arrive in the Americas until 1946, specifically in New York City, coming from Tel Aviv (which was under British administration at the time), with no record of them in Mexico until 1950, making it impossible for Pardo to have been born on Mexican soil. This suggests that her birth certificate was possibly forged or obtained years later through a false declaration; therefore, it is likely that Annie was actually born in Bulgaria, her parents’ country of origin, or in Tel Aviv, from where her family emigrated.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://etcetera.com.mx/nacional/madre-sheinbaum-no-mexicana-aqui-evidencias/|title=La madre de Sheinbaum no es mexicana. Aquí las evidencias|accessdate=2025-09-16|date=2024-04-05|website=Etcetera|language=es}}</ref>
